title: When the Ember Turns Again
premise: Mirabel Villalobos has survived the usurper's court for six years by making her poison immunity look like luck, but the crown's new gift-hunt forces her to flee into the Thornfell mountains with a smuggler caravan carrying a secret: a living heir of the extinguished royal line. As the hunt closes in and the usurper's armies march toward the free cities, Mirabel must choose between saving herself and reopening the Ember Gate, the last door into a kingdom that officially no longer exists. The cost of opening it is the taster's own immunity — every protection her body has bought, surrendered at once. In the end, the heir crosses into the old country to rally what remains of it, while Mirabel, stripped and mortal, stays behind to hold the mountain passes with nothing but a smuggler's knowledge of the roads.
about_author: S. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working mountain lodges across the borderlands, collecting smugglers' stories between shifts. Hartwell writes fantasy about people whose survival skills are mistaken for smallness.

chapters.title: The Sixth Dish
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At the usurper's winter court, Mirabel tastes a poisoned stew meant for a minor lord and must fake illness convincingly without revealing her gift. She notices the poison's signature — alchemists' work, meaning the crown is testing its own courtiers. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of realizing her employer is hunting people exactly like her.

chapters.title: A Hunt Proclaimed
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The usurper publicly announces the gift-hunt: immunity will be exposed, registered, and conscripted. Mirabel's handler, who has suspected her for years, gives her one night's head start — a debt called in. She flees into Thornfell with nothing but her palate and a forged pass. Emotional beat: grief for the life built on small compromises, abandoned in a single night.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. She buys passage with a caravan led by Dax Ferrow, a one-eyed smuggler who charges double for secrets. Mid-mountain, the caravan is stopped by gift-hunters with sniffer-hounds bred to taste poison in the air. Mirabel masks the whole caravan with bitterroot smoke. Emotional beat: the first flicker of belonging — being useful to people who don't own her.

chapters.title: What the Wagon Carries
chapters.summary: POV Dax. Dax reveals the caravan's true cargo: a sickly nineteen-year-old, Emeric, the last grandson of the old dynasty, hidden in a spice wagon for three years. The hunt isn't for smugglers — it's a dragnet for him, and the hounds caught his scent. Emotional beat: Dax's guilt at having lied to the caravan, and his grudging respect for Mirabel's nerve.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Hunted through the high passes, Mirabel leads them along smuggler roads that predate the usurper — roads that only exist for those who remember the old kingdom's names. Emeric, raised in hiding, knows the old names better than she does. Emotional beat: the strange intimacy of strangers building trust through shared competence.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Close Their Gates
chapters.summary: POV Dax. The caravan reaches the lowlands to find the free cities sealing their walls against refugees, bribed into neutrality by the usurper. There is no asylum left. Dax's old contacts refuse him one by one. Emotional beat: the collapse of the smuggler's creed that every road leads somewhere open.

chapters.title: The Ember Gate
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. An old taster's legend points to the Ember Gate — a door in the mountains into the old country, sealed when the dynasty fell, openable only by royal blood and a body freely offered. Mirabel realizes her immunity, built dish by dish, is the price: the gate drinks protection from a willing body. Emotional beat: terror and strange relief at finally seeing what her survival is worth.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Dax. The gift-hunters, led by the handler who spared Mirabel, corner the caravan in a burned waystation. He offers Mirabel registration and safety if she surrenders Emeric. She refuses; a fight breaks out; Dax takes a crossbow bolt meant for the boy. Emotional beat: the handler's genuine regret, and Dax bleeding out while insisting the plan go on without him.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At the Gate, Mirabel offers herself. The door takes her immunity in a fever of unmaking — six years of protection stripped in minutes, every poison she ever survived re-echoing through her body. Emeric crosses into the old country as the gate seals. Emotional beat: agony transfigured into choice; she is, at last, simply mortal and free.

chapters.title: What the Mountains Hold
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, months later. The usurper's armies stall in the passes, bled by smugglers who now fight under Mirabel's road-knowledge. News crosses the mountains: the old country is stirring behind its sealed door. Mirabel, immune no longer, tastes her food carefully like anyone else — and finds she doesn't miss it. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; survival redefined as something shared rather than hoarded.
